outputs.exact_statement: For every integer $d\ge3$ and every $\beta\ge0$, the free zero-field Ising law $\mu_{d,\beta}$ is a factor of IID in the sense of [eq:equivariance] if and only if $$\tanh\beta\le(d-1)^{-1/2}.$$ In this range the factor can be chosen to commute with every automorphism on every label input.

For a fixed deterministic time $t\ge0$, set $$m_v(t)=\mathbb E[\sigma_v\mid\mathcal F_t^0],\qquad
 m_{v\to w}(t)
   =\mathbb E[\sigma_v\mid\mathcal F_t^{T_{v\to w}}].$$ These means lie in $(-1,1)$ almost surely. Write $h_v=\operatorname{atanh}m_v$ and $h_{v\to w}=\operatorname{atanh}m_{v\to w}$, and define $$\psi(z)=\operatorname{atanh}(\theta\tanh z),\qquad
 a(z)=\frac{1-\tanh^2z}{1-\theta^2\tanh^2z}.$$ At each fixed time, almost surely, $$\label{eq:cavity}
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{v\to w}(t)
   &=X_v(t)+\sum_{\substack{u\sim v\\u\ne w}}
                       \psi(h_{u\to v}(t)),\\
 h_v(t)
   &=X_v(t)+\sum_{u\sim v}\psi(h_{u\to v}(t))
     =h_{v\to w}(t)+\psi(h_{w\to v}(t)).
 \end{aligned}$$ The fields have causal, progressively measurable Borel versions as functions of the observation paths. The component version uses only paths in $T_{v\to w}$. These versions require no distinguished root and satisfy, at every input and time, $$\label{eq:site-field-bound}
 |h_v(t)-X_v(t)|\le d\beta,\qquad
 |h_{v\to w}(t)-X_v(t)|\le b\beta.$$ In the process formulas below, use these chosen field versions and set $m_v(t)=\tanh h_v(t)$ and $m_{v\to w}(t)=\tanh h_{v\to w}(t)$. For the simple path $v=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_r=u$, define $$\label{eq:covariance}
 \begin{aligned}
 c_{vu}(t)
   &=\theta^r\prod_{i=1}^r
                  a(h_{v_i\to v_{i-1}}(t)),&
 c_{vv}(t)&=1,\\
 C_{vu}(t)&=(1-m_v(t)^2)c_{vu}(t).
 \end{aligned}$$ The last expression is a progressively measurable version of $\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(\sigma_v,\sigma_u\mid\mathcal F_t^0)$ at each fixed time. The cavity and covariance formulas also hold in every finite connected subtree, with branches restricted to that subtree. For all real $z$, $$0<a(z)\le1,\qquad |\psi(z)|\le\beta,\qquad
 \psi'(z)=\theta a(z)\in(0,\theta],$$ and $0\le C_{vu}(t)\le\theta^{\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(v,u)}$ at each fixed time.

There are constants $c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, such that for every $t>0$ and every vertex $v$, $$\label{eq:critical-information}
 c\omega(t)\le M(t)\le C\omega(t),
 \qquad
 \mathbb Em_v(t)^2\le C\omega(t).$$ One may take $c=1/5$. In particular both upper bounds are $C\sqrt t$ for $0<t\le1$.

For every integrable function $f(Y)$ and $\eta\in\{-1,1\}$, $$\label{eq:component-field-tilts}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E[f(Y)\mid\sigma_v=\eta]
   &=\mathbb E[f(Y)(1+\eta\tanh Y)],\\
 \mathbb E[f(Y)\mid\sigma_w=\eta]
   &=\mathbb E[f(Y)(1+\eta\theta\tanh Y)].
 \end{aligned}$$ In particular either conditioning leaves the expectation of every integrable even function of $Y$ unchanged.

There is $c_0>0$, depending only on $d$, such that for every $t>0$, every $z\in\mathbb R$, and $\eta\in\{-1,1\}$, $$\label{eq:shifted-attenuation}
 \mathbb E\left[
   a\bigl(z+\psi(h_{v\to w}(t))\bigr)^2
       \,\middle|\,\sigma_w=\eta\right]
 \le1-c_0\omega(t).$$ For every deterministic simple path $v_0,\ldots,v_r$, $r\ge1$, $$\label{eq:conditional-path-attenuation}
 \mathbb E\left[
   \prod_{i=1}^r a(h_{v_i\to v_{i-1}}(t))^2
       \,\middle|\,\sigma_{v_0},\ldots,\sigma_{v_r}\right]
 \le e^{-c_0\omega(t)r}.$$ The same bound holds for the reverse product $\prod_{i=1}^r a(h_{v_{i-1}\to v_i}(t))^2$, and both bounds also hold without conditioning on the path spins.

If $Y$ is a continuous square-integrable martingale in $(\mathcal G_t^0)$ and is continuous in $L^2$ at each time, then it is also a martingale in $(\mathcal G_t)$. More generally, if $Z$ is integrable and a version $M(t)=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal G_t^0]$ is continuous in $L^1$, then $M(t)=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal G_t]$ at every fixed time.

For every $\delta>0$ there is $\kappa_\delta\in(0,1)$ such that, for every finite connected subtree $D$, every $v,u\in D$, and every $s\ge\delta$, $$\label{eq:gaussian-path-tail}
 \mathbb E[C_{vu}^D(s)^2]
     \le\theta^{2r}(1-\kappa_\delta)^r,
       \qquad r=\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(v,u).$$ The same inequality holds for the whole-tree covariance $C_{vu}(s)$.

For fixed $v,u$ and $T<\infty$, each of $C_{vu}$ and $c_{vu}$ is the $L^2([0,T]\times\Omega,\,\mathrm ds\,\,\mathrm d\mathbb P)$ limit of bounded elementary processes $$G(s)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\xi_j\mathbf1_{(t_j,t_{j+1}]}(s),
 \qquad 0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T,$$ where $\xi_j$ is a bounded Borel function of finitely many observations at time $t_j$. In particular each coefficient has a predictable representative for stochastic integration.

The law [eq:copy-law] is invariant under the simultaneous action of each fixed automorphism of $T_d$. Every finite subvector of $W$ is standard vector Brownian motion in $(\mathcal H_t)$. For each copy $j$, both equations [eq:magnetization-sde] and [eq:field-sde] hold in this filtration, with the coefficients of that copy and the common Brownian motions $W$. Their infinite Brownian sums converge in the maximal $L^2$ norm on every finite time interval.

Let $d\ge3$, $b=d-1$, and $0<\theta\le b^{-1/2}$. Let $\pi$ be a probability law on $\mathsf X^2$ with both marginals equal to $\nu$, invariant under the simultaneous action of $\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(T_d)$. Suppose that $g=(g_e)$ assigns a measurable real function of $\mathsf X$ to every directed edge, with $\mathbb E_\nu g_e^2<\infty$, and that for each fixed $\gamma\in\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(T_d)$ and directed edge $e$, $$g_{\gamma e}(\gamma x)=g_e(x) \quad\text{for \(\nu\)-almost every \(x\)}.$$ Here $\gamma(i,j)=(\gamma i,\gamma j)$. For the two coordinate arrays $X,X'$ under $\pi$, set $$D_e=g_e(X)-g_e(X'),\qquad S=\mathbb E_\pi D_e^2.$$ The value of $S$ is independent of the directed edge. There is a constant $C_d<\infty$, depending only on $d$, such that for every integer $r\ge1$ and every simple path $v_0,\ldots,v_r$, $$\label{eq:path-variance} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E_\pi\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^rD_{(v_{i-1},v_i)}\right)^2\right] &\le C_d rS,\\ \mathbb E_\pi\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^rD_{(v_i,v_{i-1})}\right)^2\right] &\le C_d rS. \end{aligned}$$ In particular, take $\pi$ to be the $(X,X')$-marginal of the joining in Proposition 13. Then this holds for the differences $D_e(t)$ in [eq:log-discrepancy-def] at each fixed finite time, with $S=S(t)$.

For the full observation law $\nu$, the spectrum of $\mathsf A_\nu$ on centered vertex assignments is contained in $[-\rho,\rho]$, where $$\label{eq:spectrum-rho}
 \rho=\frac{2\sqrt b}{d}<1.$$

Set $$\eta=\min\left\{\frac{c_0}{4},\frac{\log b}{8}\right\},\qquad

 \label{eq:double-exp}$$ The constants depend only on $d$ and are uniform in the time, vertex, first-step restriction, and orientation.

There are constants $0<K<\infty$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $d$, such that for every integer $p\ge1$ and every $0<t\le t_0$, $$\mathbb E|h_{v\to w}(t)|^p\le e^{Kp^2}t^{p/4}.
 \label{eq:critical-all-moments}$$ There are also $c>0$ and $t_{\mathrm{tail}}\in(0,t_0]$ such that $$\mathbb P\bigl(|h_{v\to w}(t)|>t^{1/8}\bigr)
 \le \exp\bigl(-c\log^2(1/t)\bigr),
 \qquad 0<t\le t_{\mathrm{tail}}.
 \label{eq:critical-field-tail}$$ Both inequalities hold as well when conditioned on either value of the component-root spin $\sigma_v$, or on either value of the deleted-neighbor spin $\sigma_w$.

There is a fixed $t_*\in(0,\min\{t_{\mathrm{tail}},e^{-1}\}]$ such that, for $0<t\le\min\{t_*,T\}$ with $V(t)>0$, $$S(t)\le C_T V(t)
   \left(t^{1/4}+\frac{I(t)}{\log^2(1/t)}\right).
 \label{eq:small-log-loss}$$ At every time in $[0,T]$, the bound $S(t)\le CV(t)$ remains valid.
For the invariant conditional coupling with common innovations at $\theta=b^{-1/2}$, the site-field discrepancy satisfies $V(t)=0$ for every $t\ge0$.
